title: Scope of Article 2 and mixed transactions
shortTitle: Scope of Article 2 and mixed transactions
summary: Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code supplies statutory rules for transactions in goods. Identifying its scope determines which formation, interpretation, and remedial rules govern.
notes:
The casebook defines goods through movability and examines transactions combining goods with services or other property. It describes the predominant-purpose approach and competing methods for mixed transactions, then identifies proposed 2022 amendments in their publication context. Article 2 does not resolve every issue: § 1-103 permits other legal and equitable principles to supplement provisions unless displaced. The CISG can govern qualifying international sales. A party’s merchant status affects particular UCC provisions and is a separate question from whether Article 2 applies at all.

The text compares a goods sale with installation, a navigation device with continuing services, and the sale of a radio business containing both goods and other assets. Bonebrake uses predominant purpose; Foster separates portions; Anthony Pools looks to the gravamen of the particular claim. The book then reproduces 2022 amendments addressing hybrid transactions and explicitly notes that enactment was at an early stage in April 2023. This update reports that publication-time status and makes no claim about enactment in 2026.
